title: SteadyFlow harness — field notes and runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic field notebook for the new "SteadyFlow" throughput harness we ran across multiple clusters. Intent: capture observed failure modes (not all covered in the formal playbooks), a hardened loadgen config we found stable, and heuristics for warmup + repeatability that differ from the standard priming checklist.

High-level summary: 
- SteadyFlow focuses on maintaining a controlled, occupancy-driven steady-state rather than purely time-based warmup.
- Primary knobs: client pacing jitter, soft-occupancy target, KV-cache retention windows, and incremental token-length mixing.
- Key observations from runs: GPU occupancy oscillations often correlate with client-side microburst alignment; thermal throttling occurred on two racks when occupancy > 95% for > 90s.
- Resulting recommendation: use a 3-stage ramp (seed -> occupancy-targeting -> stabilizer), with a short cooling window between high-occupancy sweeps.

Experiment context and constraints:
- Cluster: 8x A100-80GB per shard, mixed 2-shard and 4-shard config across tests.
- Model: rw-large-v2 (int8/kv-cache enabled), typical seq_len 512, avg output 64 tokens.
- Baseline target: 10k tok/s per GPU aggregate, SLO: p95 latency < 120ms for single-token streaming.
- Time window: runs executed during off-hours (02:00–06:00) to reduce noisy co-tenancy; still saw variance.

SteadyFlow harness outline (conceptual):
1) Seed stage (2–4 minutes): low-rate, representative prompts to populate KV-cache and JIT code paths. Use deterministic RNG seed for request bodies.
2) Occupancy-drive stage (6–12 minutes): automated controller measures GPU util and adjusts client pacing to hit a target occupancy (e.g., 72% / 85% / 95%). Controller uses exponential smoothing on occupancy readings (alpha=0.3).
3) Stabilizer stage (4–8 minutes): lock pacing, collect telemetry for final 3 minutes. If occupancy jitter > 5% stddev then auto-run up to 2 additional short sweeps.
4) Cooldown (optional): a 60s drop to 20% pacing to allow thermal and memory stabilisation before final capture if long-run.

Why occupancy targeting?
- We found token-throughput correlates better with sustained kernel occupancy (SM utilization + memory bandwidth) than request rate alone.
- Pure rate-based warmup overshoots and produces microburst locking/unlocking that inflates latency tail.

Loadgen config (recommended defaults) — this is the JSON payload used by the harness: 
{
  "clients": 48,
  "qps_per_client": 6,
  "pacing_jitter_pct": 12,
  "sequence_mix": ["256:0.6","512:0.3","1024:0.1"],
  "rng_seed": 42,
  "occupancy_targets": [72,85,95],
  "occupancy_smoothing_alpha": 0.3,
  "kv_cache_retention_s": 600,
  "cooldown_s": 60
}
(Notes: keep rng_seed stable across repeated experiments that require deterministic request payloads; use variable seeds for runs testing input entropy effects.)

Repeatability controls (practical checklist):
- Fixed artifacts: same git commit tag of serving-runtime + model artifact sha.
- Controlled artifacts: client image digest, loadgen flags (above), and system KMS/driver versions recorded.
- Environmental controls: no scheduled autoscaling events, disable cluster backups during run, record thermal baseline.
- Data collection: record per-GPU SM utilization, mem bw, nvlink counters, CPU load, process RSS, and kernel-level timelines (profiling hooks).
- Seed management: run 3 baseline seeds (42, 31415, 7) and report mean + stdev. 

Warmup heuristics we found useful (deviations from older playbooks):
- Don't rely on wall-clock time alone — use occupancy and cache-hit ratio as gates to transition stages.
- If KV-cache warmup is slow (cache-hit < 40% after seed stage), extend seed stage and add a short focused prefix sequence that hits common tokens.
- When testing quantized kernels, include a dedicated short run that forces code-paths for int8 fallback to avoid late path JITing during the main capture.

Observed failure modes and mitigations (field notes):
1) Microburst alignment: clients with identical pacing bursts lined up lead to 200–400ms p99 spikes. Mitigation: add 8–15% random jitter to inter-request timers and stagger client start times by 1–3s.
2) KV-cache churn: aggressive sequence-mix with many long sequences caused cache thrash. Mitigation: set kv_cache_retention_s to >= 600s for benchmark runs or reduce long-seq fraction during occupancy drive.
3) Thermal trips on racks: continuous occupancy >95% for >90s raised GPU clocks down. Mitigation: insert cooldown or cap occupancy sweep duration.
4) Driver jitter: rare kernel driver stalls observed correlated with concurrent system daemon updates; ensure driver/OS patch windows disabled during runs.

Observability checklist (what we snapshot):
- Raw loadgen: QPS histogram, inter-arrival CDF, request size distribution.
- Serving runtime: token/sec counters, batching stats, KV hit rate, active cache entries.
- Host/GPU: nvidia-smi sampling (1s), nvprof traces for suspect runs, GPU thermal and clock logs.
- Network: p95/p99 egress latency between client and shard nodes.
- Logs: runtime GC/eviction events, batch formation logs, scheduling preemption events.

Sample run log (shortened):
- run_id: steadyflow-2025-11-12-03a
- config: clients=48 qps=288 total_target_tokens=10M occupancy_target=85
- seed stage: 3:20, kv_hit rose from 6% -> 58%
- occupancy stage: reached 84.7% after 2m12s (controller ramped pacing +6%)
- stabilizer: p95 latency 108ms, p99 220ms (microburst tail present)
- notes: second stabilizer sweep reduced p99 to 175ms; cooldown avoided a thermal dip seen on earlier sweep.

Acceptance criteria for a stable capture: (pass all)
- occupancy within +/-3% for final 3 minutes
- kv_cache_hit >= 55% (or documented rationale for lower)
- p95 token latency within SLO and p99 tail reduced by < 20% vs baseline
- no driver or node-level thermal events recorded

Quick commands and snippets (for engineers):
- start harness controller: ./steadyflow-controller --config run.yaml --outdir /tmp/steadyflow-runs/$(date +%s)
- sample nvtop overlay: nvtop -s 1 --filter "a100" > nvtop-sample.log &
- extract final capture: python tools/pack_capture.py --run /tmp/steadyflow-runs/12345 --out artifacts/12345.tgz

Open questions / follow-ups: 
- How does SteadyFlow interact with dynamic batching when multiple model versions are enabled on the same shard? (ENG-1423 notes; need short study.)
- Probe mixed-precision transitions: measure int8->fp16 fallback rate under long-tail sequences.
- Consider automating an adaptive cooldown heuristic that monitors GPU clocks and inserts drops proactively.

Appendix: short YAML template for runs (copyable)
---
clients: 48
qps_per_client: 6
pacing_jitter_pct: 12
sequence_mix:
  - {len: 256, weight: 0.6}
  - {len: 512, weight: 0.3}
  - {len: 1024, weight: 0.1}
rng_seed: 42
occupancy_targets: [72, 85, 95]
occupancy_smoothing_alpha: 0.3
kv_cache_retention_s: 600
cooldown_s: 60
---

Last notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic — a complement to the formal playbooks. If you run this harness, paste logs into the linked ENG-1423 ticket and flag any anomalies in #eng-serving-runtime.

Author: Ava Chen
Regards,
